records.source: וּמַֽלְכַּת־שְׁבָ֗א שָֽׁמְעָה֮ אֶת־שֵׁ֣מַע שְׁלֹמֹה֒ וַתָּב֣וֹא לְנַסּוֹת֩ אֶת־שְׁלֹמֹ֨ה בְחִיד֜וֹת בִּירֽוּשָׁלִַ֗ם בְּחַ֣יִל כָּבֵ֣ד מְאֹ֡ד וּ֠גְמַלִּים נֹשְׂאִ֨ים בְּשָׂמִ֧ים וְזָהָ֛ב לָרֹ֖ב וְאֶ֣בֶן יְקָרָ֑ה וַתָּבוֹא֙ אֶל־שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וַתְּדַבֵּ֣ר עִמּ֔וֹ אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה עִם־לְבָבָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And [the] queen of Sheba heard [the] report of Solomon, and she came to test Solomon with riddles in Jerusalem, with [a] retinue heavy very and camels carrying spices and gold in abundance and stone precious; and she came to Solomon and she spoke with him all that was with her heart.
pieces: The queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's fame, and she came to Jerusalem to test Solomon with difficult questions. She came with a very large company, with camels carrying spices, a great quantity of gold, and precious stones. When she came to Solomon, she talked with him about everything she had on her mind.

L.1: And the queen of Sheba heard the report of Solomon, and she came to test Solomon with riddles in Jerusalem, with a very heavy retinue and camels carrying spices and gold in abundance and precious stones; and she came to Solomon and spoke with him all that was with her heart.

R.1: The queen of Sheba heard how famous Solomon was. So she came to Jerusalem to test him with hard questions. She arrived with a huge group of attendants. Her camels were loaded with spices, large amounts of gold, and valuable jewels. She came to Solomon and asked him about everything she had been thinking about.

decisions.choice: the same visit as 1 Kings 10:1-2, told a little more briefly
decisions.reason: Verses 1-28 retell 1 Kings 10:1-29 almost word for word. Here Chronicles does not have the words "concerning the name of Yahweh" that Kings adds to Solomon's fame, and it joins the queen's coming and her arrival in Jerusalem into one sentence. The visit and its purpose are the same.

decisions.choice: Sheba: a trading kingdom in the south of Arabia
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:1, Sheba lay in the south-west of the Arabian peninsula and grew rich on the caravan trade in incense, spices, gold and precious stones, the goods the queen brings here (Psalm 72:10, 15; Isaiah 60:6).

decisions.choice: riddles: hard, puzzling questions; a very heavy retinue: a large company of attendants
decisions.reason: The first word names a riddle that has to be worked out (Judges 14:12-19; Proverbs 1:6); testing a ruler with such questions probed his wisdom, the gift God gave Solomon (1:10-12). The second word can mean strength, wealth or an army; here it is the people, animals and goods traveling with her, "heavy" meaning great in number.

decisions.choice: all that was with her heart: everything she had in mind to ask
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought in Hebrew. She laid before Solomon all the questions she had prepared.

decisions.choice: riddles (Literal); difficult questions (Balanced); hard questions (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:1: Literal keeps the narrow sense of the word, and Balanced and Readable say "questions", since "riddles" can sound like children's games.

decisions.choice: a huge group of attendants; valuable jewels
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:2, Readable names who made up the company and says "jewels" for "precious stones".

records.heading: The queen of Sheba

records.source: וַיַּגֶּד־לָ֥הּ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה אֶת־כָּל־דְּבָרֶ֑יהָ וְלֹֽא־נֶעְלַ֤ם דָּבָר֙ מִשְּׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹ֦א הִגִּ֖יד לָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And told her Solomon all her words, and not was hidden [a] word from Solomon which not he told her.
pieces: Solomon answered all her questions; nothing was too hidden for Solomon to explain to her.

L.2: And Solomon told her all her words, and there was not a thing hidden from Solomon that he did not tell her.

R.2: Solomon answered every one of her questions. None of them was too hard for him to explain.

decisions.choice: told her all her words: answered every question she put to him
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:3, the verb means to tell or make known; with "her words", the questions she raised, it means that Solomon gave her the answer to each one.

decisions.choice: hidden from Solomon: beyond his understanding
decisions.reason: A matter "hidden" from someone is one he cannot see into. None of her riddles was beyond Solomon's grasp. Where 1 Kings 10:3 says "hidden from the king", Chronicles names him: "hidden from Solomon"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: answered; explain
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:3, the same verb appears twice; Balanced and Readable say "answered" for the first and "explain" for the second.

records.source: וַתֵּ֨רֶא֙ מַֽלְכַּת־שְׁבָ֔א אֵ֖ת חָכְמַ֣ת שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וְהַבַּ֖יִת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And saw [the] queen of Sheba [the] wisdom of Solomon, and the house which he built,
pieces: When the queen of Sheba saw Solomon's wisdom, and the palace he had built,

L.3: And the queen of Sheba saw the wisdom of Solomon, and the house that he had built,

R.3: The queen of Sheba saw for herself how wise Solomon was. She saw the palace he had built.

decisions.choice: saw: the sentence runs on to the end of verse 4
decisions.reason: Verses 3 and 4 are one sentence: a list of what the queen saw, ending with how it affected her ("there was no more spirit in her"). 1 Kings 10:4 has "all the wisdom of Solomon"; Chronicles has "the wisdom of Solomon", with the same sense.

decisions.choice: the house that he had built: Solomon's palace
decisions.reason: "House" can mean a palace or a temple. Since the house of Yahweh is named at the end of verse 4, this house is most likely the royal palace Solomon built (8:1).

decisions.choice: palace
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:4, Balanced and Readable say "palace" for "house", so that readers do not take it for the house of the LORD.

records.source: וּמַאֲכַ֣ל שֻׁלְחָנ֡וֹ וּמוֹשַׁ֣ב עֲבָדָיו֩ וּמַעֲמַ֨ד מְשָׁרְתָ֜יו וּמַלְבּֽוּשֵׁיהֶ֗ם וּמַשְׁקָיו֙ וּמַלְבּ֣וּשֵׁיהֶ֔ם וַעֲלִיָּת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲלֶ֖ה בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹא־הָ֥יָה ע֛וֹד בָּ֖הּ רֽוּחַ׃
records.gloss: and [the] food of his table, and [the] seating of his servants, and [the] standing of his attendants and their clothing, and his cupbearers and their clothing, and his burnt offering which he offered up [at the] house of Yahweh, and not was in her still spirit.
pieces: the food on his table, the seating of his officials, the service of his attendants and their robes, his cupbearers and their robes, and the burnt offerings he offered at the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, she was left breathless.

L.4: and the food of his table, and the seating of his servants, and the standing of his attendants and their clothing, and his cupbearers and their clothing, and his burnt offerings that he offered up [at the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, then there was no more spirit in her.

R.4: She saw the food on his table, the way his officials were seated, how his servants waited on him, and the fine clothes they wore. She saw his cupbearers and their fine clothes, and the burnt offerings he sacrificed at the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It all took her breath away.

decisions.choice: his burnt offerings that he offered up at the house of Yahweh, read as in 1 Kings 10:5
alternatives: his ascent by which he went up to the house of Yahweh
decisions.reason: Where 1 Kings 10:5 has the word for "burnt offering", Chronicles has a related word that elsewhere means an upper room or a going up, and its vowels make the verb "he went up". Read that way, the phrase is "his ascent by which he went up to the house of Yahweh", the stairway or procession by which the king went to the temple, and some ancient translations read it so. The two accounts tell the same scene, and this translation reads Chronicles as it reads Kings, of the offerings the king brought at the temple, as an ancient translation of Chronicles also does. The other reading is just as possible.

decisions.choice: there was no more spirit in her: she was overwhelmed
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:5, "spirit" is breath and strength; to have none left is to be stunned. Here it is amazement, not fear.

decisions.choice: his servants, his attendants, his cupbearers: the members of Solomon's court
decisions.reason: "Servants" here are the king's officials, seated in order at his table; the attendants stood ready to serve, and the cupbearers served the king's wine (Nehemiah 1:11). Chronicles mentions the cupbearers' clothing as well, which 1 Kings 10:5 does not.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: As with the king's servants elsewhere in these books, Balanced and Readable say "officials" for men who held posts at court.

decisions.choice: she was left breathless (Balanced); It all took her breath away (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:5, Literal keeps the Hebrew picture; Balanced and Readable use the English idiom of breath.

records.source: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֱמֶת֙ הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי בְּאַרְצִ֑י עַל־דְּבָרֶ֖יךָ וְעַל־חָכְמָתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And she said to the king, Truth [is] the word which I heard in my land about your words and about your wisdom.
pieces: She said to the king, "It is true, the report that reached me in my own country about your words and your wisdom.

L.5: And she said to the king, "True [is] the word that I heard in my land about your words and about your wisdom.

R.5: She said to the king, "Everything I heard in my own country about what you have said and how wise you are is true.

decisions.choice: true is the report: the word "truth" comes first for emphasis
decisions.reason: The queen begins with the word "truth": what she had heard and half doubted (verse 6) has proved true. 1 Kings 10:6 says "true was the report"; Chronicles leaves out "was", which Hebrew may do, and the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: your words: what Solomon said
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:6, the word can mean words or matters. Paired with "your wisdom", it most likely means his sayings and answers, though it could also take in his affairs and achievements.

decisions.choice: word (Literal); report (Balanced); Everything I heard (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word for "word" here means a report, as the verb "heard" shows. Balanced says "report" and Readable puts it as what she heard, as at 1 Kings 10:6.

records.source: וְלֹֽא־הֶאֱמַ֣נְתִּי לְדִבְרֵיהֶ֗ם עַ֤ד אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֨אתִי֙ וַתִּרְאֶ֣ינָה עֵינַ֔י וְהִנֵּה֙ לֹ֣א הֻגַּד־לִ֔י חֲצִ֖י מַרְבִּ֣ית חָכְמָתֶ֑ךָ יָסַ֕פְתָּ עַל־הַשְּׁמוּעָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמָֽעְתִּי׃
records.gloss: And not I believed their words until that I came and saw my eyes, and look, not was told to me [the] half of [the] greatness of your wisdom; you have added to the report which I heard.
pieces: But I did not believe what they said until I came and saw it with my own eyes. And indeed, I was not told even half of how great your wisdom is. You go far beyond the report I heard.

L.6: And I did not believe their words until I came and my eyes saw; and look, the half of the greatness of your wisdom was not told to me. You have added beyond the report that I heard.

R.6: But I did not believe them until I came and saw it for myself. Now I see that they did not tell me even half of how wise you are! You are far greater than the reports I heard.

decisions.choice: differences from 1 Kings 10:7
decisions.reason: Kings has "the words" where Chronicles has "their words", the reports others brought her. Kings says "the half was not told to me" and "you have added wisdom and good"; Chronicles says "the half of the greatness of your wisdom" was not told her, and simply "you have added". Chronicles puts the weight on Solomon's wisdom; the sense of her words is the same.

decisions.choice: look: she points to what she now sees
decisions.reason: The small word draws attention to something seen or realized. The queen turns from what she heard to what is before her eyes.

decisions.choice: you have added beyond the report: you surpass what was said of you
decisions.reason: To "add to" a report is to go beyond it. The reality is more than the rumor.

decisions.choice: indeed (Balanced); Now I see (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:7, neither level uses the old word "behold"; Balanced says "indeed" and Readable puts her surprise in her own words.

records.source: אַשְׁרֵ֣י אֲנָשֶׁ֔יךָ וְאַשְׁרֵ֖י עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ אֵ֑לֶּה הָעֹמְדִ֤ים לְפָנֶ֨יךָ֙ תָּמִ֔יד וְשֹׁמְעִ֖ים אֶת־חָכְמָתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Happy your men, and happy your servants these, the standing before you continually and hearing your wisdom.
pieces: How happy your men must be! How happy are these officials of yours, who stand before you all the time and hear your wisdom!

L.7: Happy [are] your men, and happy [are] these your servants who stand before you continually and hear your wisdom.

R.7: How fortunate your men are! How fortunate these officials are, who are always with you and get to hear your wisdom!

decisions.choice: happy: fortunate, well off
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:8, the word describes a person whose lot is good (Psalm 1:1). It is not the word for being blessed by God that the queen uses in verse 8.

decisions.choice: your men
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "your men" here and in 1 Kings 10:8, which this verse repeats. The ancient Greek translation of Kings has "your wives", which differs by one letter in Hebrew. "Your men" fits the next line, about the officials who serve the king.

decisions.choice: who stand before you: who serve you
decisions.reason: To stand before a king is to be in his service, waiting on his word (1 Kings 1:2; 12:8).

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: As in verse 4, Balanced and Readable say "officials" for the king's servants at court.

records.source: יְהִ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ בָּר֔וּךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀חָפֵ֣ץ בְּךָ֗ לְתִתְּךָ֤ עַל־כִּסְאוֹ֙ לְמֶ֔לֶךְ לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ בְּאַהֲבַ֨ת אֱלֹהֶ֤יךָ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְהַעֲמִיד֣וֹ לְעוֹלָ֔ם וַיִּתֶּנְךָ֤ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ לְמֶ֔לֶךְ לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת מִשְׁפָּ֥ט וּצְדָקָֽה׃
records.gloss: May be Yahweh your God blessed, who delighted in you to put you on his throne as king for Yahweh your God; in [the] loving of your God Israel to establish it forever, and he set you over them as king to do justice and righteousness.
pieces: Blessed be {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, who has delighted in you and set you on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} throne as king for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God! Because your God loves Israel and would make it stand firm forever, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made you king over them, to do justice and righteousness."

L.8: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God be blessed, who delighted in you to set you on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} throne as king for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God! Because your God loved Israel, to establish it forever, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} set you over them as king to do justice and righteousness."

R.8: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God! He was pleased with you and put you on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own throne to rule as king for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Your God loves Israel and wants to keep it secure forever, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made you king over them to rule with justice and righteousness."

decisions.choice: differences from 1 Kings 10:9
decisions.reason: Kings has "to set you on the throne of Israel"; Chronicles has "to set you on his throne as king for Yahweh your God". Kings has "because Yahweh loved Israel forever"; Chronicles has "because your God loved Israel, to establish it forever", and "over them" after "he set you". The queen's praise is the same, but Chronicles makes plain that the throne is God's and that his love means to keep Israel standing.

decisions.choice: his throne, as king for Yahweh your God: the king rules on God's behalf
decisions.reason: In Chronicles the kingdom belongs to Yahweh and the king sits on Yahweh's throne (1 Chronicles 17:14; 28:5; 29:23). A foreign queen speaks of Yahweh as Solomon's God, not hers, yet blesses him and credits him with Solomon's rule, as Huram did (2:11).

decisions.choice: to do justice and righteousness: to rule fairly and rightly
decisions.reason: The pair describes what a king is for: fair judgment and right dealing for all, especially the weak (2 Samuel 8:15; Psalm 72:1-4).

decisions.choice: Praise
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:9, Readable says "Praise" for "blessed", since in English to "bless" God can sound like giving him something.

decisions.choice: he set you over them as king
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins this clause with "and" after the reason; English drops the "and". The queen's speech that began in verse 5 closes here.

records.source: וַתִּתֵּ֨ן לַמֶּ֜לֶךְ מֵאָ֥ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֣ים׀כִּכַּ֣ר זָהָ֗ב וּבְשָׂמִ֛ים לָרֹ֥ב מְאֹ֖ד וְאֶ֣בֶן יְקָרָ֑ה וְלֹ֤א הָיָה֙ כַּבֹּ֣שֶׂם הַה֔וּא אֲשֶׁר־נָתְנָ֥ה מַֽלְכַּת־שְׁבָ֖א לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃
records.gloss: And she gave to the king hundred and twenty talent[s] of gold, and spices in abundance very, and stone precious; and not was like the spice the that which gave [the] queen of Sheba to the king Solomon.
pieces: Then she gave the king {{units:about 9,000 pounds|120 talents}} of gold, a very great quantity of spices, and precious stones. No spices ever matched those that the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.

L.9: And she gave to the king 120 talents of gold, and spices in very great abundance, and precious stones. And there was never spice like that which the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.

R.9: She gave the king {{units:about 9,000 pounds|120 talents}} of gold, huge amounts of spices, and valuable jewels. There had never been spices like the ones the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.

decisions.choice: 120 talents of gold: a royal gift of great size
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:10, a talent weighed about 75 pounds, so the gold weighed about 9,000 pounds. Gifts between rulers showed honor and wealth on both sides.

decisions.choice: there was never spice like that: a difference from 1 Kings 10:10
decisions.reason: Kings says that never again did such an abundance of spice come in. Chronicles says only that there was no spice like hers, which may speak of its quality as well as its amount. Both say her gift was never matched.

decisions.choice: about 9,000 pounds (talents as the alternative)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the weight in modern measure, with the Hebrew unit as the alternative; Literal keeps "talents".

records.source: וְגַם־עַבְדֵ֤י חוּרָם֙ וְעַבְדֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־הֵבִ֥יאוּ זָהָ֖ב מֵאוֹפִ֑יר הֵבִ֛יאוּ עֲצֵ֥י אַלְגּוּמִּ֖ים וְאֶ֥בֶן יְקָרָֽה׃
records.gloss: And also [the] servants of Huram and [the] servants of Solomon who brought gold from Ophir brought wood of algum and stone precious.
pieces: Huram's servants and Solomon's servants, who brought gold from Ophir, brought algum wood from there too, and precious stones.

L.10: And also the servants of Huram and the servants of Solomon, who brought gold from Ophir, brought algum wood and precious stones.

R.10: Huram's men and Solomon's men, who brought gold from Ophir, also brought back algum wood and valuable jewels.

decisions.choice: the servants of Huram and of Solomon: a difference from 1 Kings 10:11
decisions.reason: Kings speaks of "the ships of Hiram"; Chronicles speaks of the men who sailed them, Huram's sailors and Solomon's together, as 8:18 has told. Chronicles spells the king's name Huram, Kings Hiram; he is the same king of Tyre (2:2).

decisions.choice: Ophir: a distant land famous for gold
decisions.reason: Where Ophir lay is not known; places in southern Arabia, east Africa and India have all been suggested. Its gold was a byword for the finest (Job 28:16; Psalm 45:10).

decisions.choice: algum wood: a costly wood that cannot be identified with certainty
decisions.reason: Kings spells the word "almug" (1 Kings 10:11-12); Chronicles spells it "algum", as in 2:7. It was a fine wood fit for temple work and musical instruments; red sandalwood is one suggestion, but no identification is sure.

decisions.choice: men
decisions.reason: The servants here are the crews of the ships. Literal and Balanced keep "servants"; Readable says "men", since these were sailors, not household servants.

records.source: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ אֶת־עֲצֵ֨י הָֽאַלְגּוּמִּ֜ים מְסִלּ֤וֹת לְבֵית־יְהוָה֙ וּלְבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְכִנֹּר֥וֹת וּנְבָלִ֖ים לַשָּׁרִ֑ים וְלֹא־נִרְא֥וּ כָהֵ֛ם לְפָנִ֖ים בְּאֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And made the king the wood of the algum steps for [the] house of Yahweh and for [the] house of the king, and lyres and harps for the singers; and not were seen like them before in [the] land of Judah.
pieces: The king used the algum wood to make steps for the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the royal palace, as well as lyres and harps for the singers. Nothing like them had ever been seen before in the land of Judah.

L.11: And the king made the algum wood [into] steps for the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and for the house of the king, and lyres and harps for the singers; and none like them had been seen before in the land of Judah.

R.11: The king used the algum wood to make steps for the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and for the royal palace. He also made lyres and harps for the musicians. No one in the land of Judah had ever seen anything like them before.

decisions.choice: steps: some raised way or stair made of the wood
decisions.reason: The word usually means a raised road or highway. Used of buildings it may mean steps, terraces or raised walkways; its exact sense here is unknown. 1 Kings 10:12 has a different rare word, perhaps "supports" or "railings".

decisions.choice: lyres and harps: the stringed instruments of temple and court music
decisions.reason: Both are stringed instruments played by hand; the second was probably larger. David had appointed singers with such instruments for worship (1 Chronicles 15:16).

decisions.choice: none like them had been seen before in the land of Judah: a difference from 1 Kings 10:12
decisions.reason: Kings says that no such wood had come in or been seen "to this day", the writer's own day. Chronicles looks back instead: nothing like these things had been seen in Judah before Solomon made them.

decisions.choice: the temple of the LORD; musicians
decisions.reason: Readable says "temple" for the house of the LORD, and "musicians" for the singers who played these instruments, as at 1 Kings 10:12.

records.source: וְהַמֶּ֨לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה נָתַ֣ן לְמַֽלְכַּת־שְׁבָ֗א אֶת־כָּל־חֶפְצָהּ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁאָ֔לָה מִלְּבַ֖ד אֲשֶׁר־הֵבִ֣יאָה אֶל־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַֽתַּהֲפֹ֛ךְ וַתֵּ֥לֶךְ לְאַרְצָ֖הּ הִ֥יא וַעֲבָדֶֽיהָ׃פ
records.gloss: And the king Solomon gave to [the] queen of Sheba all her desire which she asked, apart from what she brought to the king; and she turned and went to her land, she and her servants.
pieces: King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she desired and asked for, more than she had brought to the king. Then she turned and went back to her own country, she and her servants.

L.12: And King Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all her desire that she asked, besides what she had brought to the king. And she turned and went to her land, she and her servants.

R.12: King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she wanted and asked for. He gave her even more than she had brought to him. Then she and her servants went back home to her own country.

decisions.choice: besides what she had brought to the king: more than the worth of her own gifts
alternatives: besides a return gift equal to what she had brought
decisions.reason: The phrase "apart from what she had brought" most likely means that Solomon's gifts were over and above the value of hers: he gave back more than he received. It could also mean that he gave her what she asked besides gifts matching what she had brought.

decisions.choice: a difference from 1 Kings 10:13
decisions.reason: Kings says Solomon gave her what she asked "besides what he gave her according to the hand of King Solomon", his royal bounty. Chronicles measures his gifts against hers instead. Both show the king giving more than was asked.

decisions.choice: all her desire that she asked: gifts in return for gifts
decisions.reason: Rulers exchanged gifts as a sign of honor and friendship. The queen had given lavishly (verse 9), and Solomon gave her whatever she asked.

decisions.choice: more than (Balanced); even more than (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the sense taken in m1 plainly; Literal keeps "besides".

records.source: וַיְהִי֙ מִשְׁקַ֣ל הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֥א לִשְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בְּשָׁנָ֣ה אֶחָ֑ת שֵׁ֥שׁ מֵא֛וֹת וְשִׁשִּׁ֥ים וָשֵׁ֖שׁ כִּכְּרֵ֥י זָהָֽב׃
records.gloss: And was [the] weight of the gold which came to Solomon in year one six hundred and sixty and six talents of gold,
pieces: The weight of the gold that came to Solomon in one year was {{units:about 50,000 pounds|666 talents}} of gold,

L.13: And the weight of the gold that came to Solomon in one year was 666 talents of gold,

R.13: In one year the gold that came to Solomon weighed {{units:about 25 tons|666 talents}}.

decisions.choice: in one year: Solomon's yearly income in gold
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:14, which this verse repeats, the phrase most likely gives a regular yearly amount. The sentence continues into verse 14, which adds income not counted in this figure.

decisions.choice: 666 talents: a vast weight of gold
decisions.reason: At about 75 pounds to the talent, this is about 50,000 pounds, about 25 tons, part of the picture of Solomon's wealth in verses 13-28.

decisions.choice: about 50,000 pounds (Balanced); about 25 tons (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:14, Balanced and Readable give the weight in modern measure, with the Hebrew unit as the alternative; Readable rounds it to tons and ends the sentence here.

records.heading: Solomon's wealth

records.source: לְבַ֞ד מֵאַנְשֵׁ֧י הַתָּרִ֛ים וְהַסֹּחֲרִ֖ים מְבִיאִ֑ים וְכָל־מַלְכֵ֤י עֲרַב֙ וּפַח֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ מְבִיאִ֛ים זָהָ֥ב וָכֶ֖סֶף לִשְׁלֹמֹֽה׃
records.gloss: apart from [the] men of the traders and the merchants [who were] bringing; and all [the] kings of Arabia and [the] governors of the land [were] bringing gold and silver to Solomon.
pieces: not counting what the traveling traders and the merchants brought in. All the kings of Arabia, and the governors of the land as well, brought gold and silver to Solomon.

L.14: apart from [what] the men of the traders and the merchants were bringing; and all the kings of Arabia and the governors of the land were bringing gold and silver to Solomon.

R.14: That did not include what traders and merchants brought in. All the kings of Arabia and the governors of the land also brought gold and silver to Solomon.

decisions.choice: the traders and the merchants: the trade that passed through Solomon's land
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:15, the first word means men who travel about, here traveling traders; the second names dealers in goods. Solomon took income from the trade routes through his kingdom.

decisions.choice: differences from 1 Kings 10:15
decisions.reason: Kings has "the kings of the Arabs", where the Hebrew letters can also be read "the mixed peoples"; Chronicles has "Arabia". Chronicles also adds that the traders "were bringing" and that the kings and governors "were bringing gold and silver to Solomon". The kings' gold and silver may be counted among the income left out of the 666 talents, as in Kings, or added as one more source; the sense of Solomon's great wealth is the same.

decisions.choice: the governors of the land: officials over districts or provinces
decisions.reason: The word names a governor of a region. These may be Solomon's own district officers or rulers of lands under his control.

decisions.choice: what (Literal, in brackets); not counting what (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "apart from the men of the traders ... bringing"; English needs a word saying that it is what they brought that was not counted.

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה מָאתַ֥יִם צִנָּ֖ה זָהָ֣ב שָׁח֑וּט שֵׁ֤שׁ מֵאוֹת֙ זָהָ֣ב שָׁח֔וּט יַעֲלֶ֖ה עַל־הַצִּנָּ֥ה הָאֶחָֽת׃
records.gloss: And made the king Solomon two hundred large-shield[s] gold beaten; six hundred gold beaten he put up on the large-shield the one.
pieces: King Solomon made 200 large shields of beaten gold, with {{units:about 15 pounds|600 shekels}} of beaten gold going into each shield.

L.15: And King Solomon made 200 large shields of beaten gold; 600 [shekels of] beaten gold he put on each large shield.

R.15: King Solomon made 200 large shields of hammered gold. Each one used {{units:about 15 pounds|600 shekels}} of gold.

decisions.choice: large shields: tall shields that covered the whole body
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:16, this word names the large shield that protected a soldier from head to foot, unlike the smaller shield of verse 16.

decisions.choice: of beaten gold: gold hammered thin, likely over a frame
decisions.reason: The gold was beaten thin and laid on the shield, probably over wood or leather. These were ceremonial shields, a display of wealth; Shishak of Egypt later carried them off (12:9-10).

decisions.choice: six hundred of gold: 600 shekels
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives only the number; the unit understood is the shekel. Chronicles repeats "beaten" with the second mention of the gold, which 1 Kings 10:16 does not; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: [shekels of] (Literal); about 15 pounds (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal supplies "shekels" in brackets; Balanced and Readable give the weight in modern measure, with "600 shekels" as the alternative. Readable leaves out the repeated "hammered".

records.source: וּשְׁלֹשׁ־מֵא֤וֹת מָֽגִנִּים֙ זָהָ֣ב שָׁח֔וּט שְׁלֹ֤שׁ מֵאוֹת֙ זָהָ֔ב יַעֲלֶ֖ה עַל־הַמָּגֵ֣ן הָאֶחָ֑ת וַיִּתְּנֵ֣ם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ בְּבֵ֖ית יַ֥עַר הַלְּבָנֽוֹן׃פ
records.gloss: And three hundred shields gold beaten; three hundred gold he put up on the shield the one; and put them the king [in the] house of [the] forest of the Lebanon.
pieces: He also made 300 shields of beaten gold, with {{units:about 7 1/2 pounds|300 shekels}} of gold going into each shield. The king placed them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.

L.16: And 300 shields of beaten gold; 300 [shekels of] gold he put on each shield. And the king put them [in the] house of the forest of Lebanon.

R.16: He also made 300 smaller shields of hammered gold. Each one used {{units:about 7 1/2 pounds|300 shekels}} of gold. The king put them in the great hall called the House of the Forest of Lebanon.

decisions.choice: shields: smaller round shields
decisions.reason: This is the common shield carried on the arm, smaller than the large shield of verse 15.

decisions.choice: 300 shekels of gold for each shield, where 1 Kings 10:17 has three minas
decisions.reason: Kings says three minas of gold went into each shield. A mina is usually reckoned at fifty shekels, which would make 150 shekels; Chronicles has 300. The two may count by different standards for the mina, or a number may have changed in copying. This translation follows the number Chronicles gives.

decisions.choice: the House of the Forest of Lebanon: Solomon's great hall
decisions.reason: This was the largest of Solomon's palace buildings, named for its rows of cedar pillars from Lebanon (1 Kings 7:2-5). It seems to have served as a hall of state and an armory (Isaiah 22:8).

decisions.choice: He also made
decisions.reason: The Hebrew continues the list from verse 15 without a verb; Balanced and Readable repeat "made". Readable says "smaller shields" to mark the difference from the large ones.

decisions.choice: about 7 1/2 pounds (300 shekels as the alternative)
decisions.reason: At about 0.4 ounce to the shekel, 300 shekels is about 7 1/2 pounds. Literal supplies "shekels" in brackets. Readable adds "the great hall called" so that the House of the Forest of Lebanon is not taken for a forest.

records.source: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ כִּסֵּא־שֵׁ֖ן גָּד֑וֹל וַיְצַפֵּ֖הוּ זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: And made the king throne of ivory great, and he overlaid it gold pure.
pieces: Then the king made a great ivory throne and overlaid it with pure gold.

L.17: And the king made a great throne of ivory, and he overlaid it [with] pure gold.

R.17: The king also made a large throne decorated with ivory and covered it with pure gold.

decisions.choice: a throne of ivory: a throne inlaid with ivory panels
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:18, ivory was carved into panels and set into wooden furniture; a throne could not be overlaid with gold if it were solid ivory (Amos 3:15).

decisions.choice: pure gold: where 1 Kings 10:18 has "refined gold"
decisions.reason: Kings uses a rarer word for the finest grade of gold; Chronicles uses the common word "pure". The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: decorated with ivory; covered
decisions.reason: Readable says how the ivory was used and says "covered" for "overlaid".

records.source: וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מַעֲל֣וֹת לַ֠כִּסֵּא וְכֶ֨בֶשׁ בַּזָּהָ֤ב לַכִּסֵּא֙ מָאֳחָזִ֔ים וְיָד֛וֹת מִזֶּ֥ה וּמִזֶּ֖ה עַל־מְק֣וֹם הַשָּׁ֑בֶת וּשְׁנַ֣יִם אֲרָי֔וֹת עֹמְדִ֖ים אֵ֥צֶל הַיָּדֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And six steps to the throne, and [a] footstool in gold to the throne [were] fastened, and hands from this and from this at [the] place of the sitting, and two lions standing beside the hands.
pieces: The throne had six steps and a footstool of gold, fastened to the throne. On either side of the seat were armrests, with two lions standing beside the armrests.

L.18: And six steps [were] to the throne, and a footstool of gold [was] to the throne, fastened [to it], and arms [were] on this [side] and on that [side] at the place of the seat, and two lions [were] standing beside the arms.

R.18: The throne had six steps leading up to it, and a gold footstool was attached to it. On each side of the seat was an armrest, and a lion statue stood beside each armrest.

decisions.choice: a footstool of gold: where 1 Kings 10:19 has "a round top behind it"
decisions.reason: Kings describes the throne's rounded back; Chronicles names a gold footstool instead. The two accounts may each mention a different part of the same throne, or one text may have been changed in copying. The rest of the description is the same.

decisions.choice: fastened: the footstool and steps were joined to the throne
alternatives: the steps and footstool were fastened together
decisions.reason: The word is plural and means "held fast" or "attached". It most likely says that the footstool (with the steps) was fixed to the throne rather than standing loose.

decisions.choice: hands: armrests
decisions.reason: The "hands" of a chair are its arms, the parts on which the sitter's hands rest.

decisions.choice: two lions: a symbol of royal power
decisions.reason: Lions often stood beside royal thrones in the ancient world; the lion was also the emblem of Judah, Solomon's tribe (Genesis 49:9).

decisions.choice: a lion statue stood beside each armrest
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the lions were carved figures, one at each side.

records.source: וּשְׁנֵ֧ים עָשָׂ֣ר אֲרָי֗וֹת עֹמְדִ֥ים שָׁ֛ם עַל־שֵׁ֥שׁ הַֽמַּעֲל֖וֹת מִזֶּ֣ה וּמִזֶּ֑ה לֹא־נַעֲשָׂ֥ה כֵ֖ן לְכָל־מַמְלָכָֽה׃
records.gloss: And two [and] ten lions standing there on [the] six the steps, from this and from this; not was made thus for any kingdom.
pieces: Twelve lions stood there on the six steps, one at each end of each step. Nothing like it had ever been made for any kingdom.

L.19: And twelve lions [were] standing there on the six steps, on this [side] and on that [side]; nothing like it was made for any kingdom.

R.19: Twelve lions stood on the six steps, one at each end of every step. No other kingdom had ever had a throne like it.

decisions.choice: twelve lions on the six steps, on this side and on that: a lion at each end of each step
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:20, which this verse repeats, six steps with a lion on either side make twelve, besides the two beside the armrests (verse 18).

decisions.choice: nothing like it was made for any kingdom: the throne was without equal
decisions.reason: The phrase claims that no other king had such a throne, part of the picture of Solomon's surpassing glory (verse 22).

decisions.choice: one at each end of each step
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out the Hebrew "from this and from this", which means on both sides of each step.

records.source: וְ֠כֹל כְּלֵ֞י מַשְׁקֵ֨ה הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה֙ זָהָ֔ב וְכֹ֗ל כְּלֵ֛י בֵּֽית־יַ֥עַר הַלְּבָנ֖וֹן זָהָ֣ב סָג֑וּר אֵ֣ין כֶּ֗סֶף נֶחְשָׁ֛ב בִּימֵ֥י שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לִמְאֽוּמָה׃
records.gloss: And all [the] vessels of drinking of the king Solomon [were] gold, and all [the] vessels of [the] house of [the] forest of the Lebanon [were] gold pure; not silver [was] reckoned in [the] days of Solomon as anything.
pieces: All King Solomon's drinking cups were gold, and all the utensils in the House of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. In Solomon's days silver was not thought of as anything.

L.20: And all the drinking vessels of King Solomon [were] gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon [were] pure gold; silver was not reckoned as anything in the days of Solomon.

R.20: All of King Solomon's cups were made of gold, and all the dishes in the House of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. In Solomon's time silver was hardly worth anything.

decisions.choice: pure gold: gold of the best quality
decisions.reason: The word describes gold that has been refined. It is used of the gold in the temple (4:20-22).

decisions.choice: silver was not reckoned as anything: there was so much wealth that silver seemed cheap
decisions.reason: A deliberate overstatement, like verse 27: silver was so common in Solomon's days that it counted for nothing.

decisions.choice: a difference from 1 Kings 10:21
decisions.reason: Kings says "there was no silver; it was not reckoned as anything". Chronicles has the shorter "silver was not reckoned as anything", though its words can also be read "none was silver; it was reckoned ...". Either way the point is the same: none of the king's vessels were silver, because silver counted for so little.

decisions.choice: hardly worth anything
decisions.reason: Readable puts "not reckoned as anything" in everyday words.

records.source: כִּֽי־אֳנִיּ֤וֹת לַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ הֹלְכ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֔ישׁ עִ֖ם עַבְדֵ֣י חוּרָ֑ם אַחַת֩ לְשָׁל֨וֹשׁ שָׁנִ֜ים תָּב֣וֹאנָה׀אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֗ישׁ נֹֽשְׂאוֹת֙ זָהָ֣ב וָכֶ֔סֶף שֶׁנְהַבִּ֥ים וְקוֹפִ֖ים וְתוּכִּיִּֽים׃פ
records.gloss: For ships [were] to the king going [to] Tarshish with [the] servants of Huram; once in three years would come [the] ships of Tarshish carrying gold and silver, ivories, and apes, and peacocks.
pieces: For the king had ships that sailed to Tarshish with Huram's servants. Once every three years the Tarshish ships would come in, bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes and peacocks.

L.21: For the king had ships going [to] Tarshish with the servants of Huram; once in three years the ships of Tarshish would come, carrying gold and silver, ivory, and apes, and peacocks.

R.21: This was because the king had ships that sailed to Tarshish with Huram's men. Once every three years these large trading ships came back loaded with gold, silver, ivory, apes and peacocks.

decisions.choice: ships going to Tarshish with Huram's servants: a difference from 1 Kings 10:22
decisions.reason: Kings says the king had "ships of Tarshish" at sea "with the ships of Hiram". "Ships of Tarshish" was a name for large seagoing merchant ships, whatever their route; Jehoshaphat built such ships to go to Ophir (1 Kings 22:49). Chronicles says the ships were "going to Tarshish", a far-off port probably in the far west of the Mediterranean (Jonah 1:3), and it names Huram's sailors rather than his ships. It may take Tarshish as the destination, or use "going to Tarshish" for the long voyages such ships made; the second half of the verse still calls them "ships of Tarshish".

decisions.choice: once in three years: a voyage that took three years to complete
decisions.reason: The ships came back once every three years, which suggests long voyages to distant places.

decisions.choice: ivory, apes, and peacocks: exotic goods whose names are not all certain
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:22, the word for ivory seems to mean "elephant tooth" and the word taken as "apes" names some kind of monkey. The last word appears only here and in Kings; it has long been taken as peacocks, but it may name baboons or another animal.

decisions.choice: This was because; Huram's men; these large trading ships
decisions.reason: Readable makes the "for" explicit as the reason for Solomon's wealth in gold, says "men" for the sailors, as in verse 10, and explains "ships of Tarshish" by the kind of ship they were.

records.source: וַיִּגְדַּל֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה מִכֹּ֖ל מַלְכֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ לְעֹ֖שֶׁר וְחָכְמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And became great the king Solomon more than all [the] kings of the earth in wealth and wisdom.
pieces: So King Solomon grew greater in riches and in wisdom than all the kings of the earth.

L.22: And King Solomon became greater than all the kings of the earth in wealth and wisdom.

R.22: King Solomon became richer and wiser than any other king on earth.

decisions.choice: wealth and wisdom: what God promised at Gibeon
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 1 Kings 10:23. Solomon had asked for wisdom, and God promised him riches and honor as well, such as no king before or after him would have (1:11-12). This verse records that the promise was kept.

decisions.choice: became greater: Solomon grew to surpass all other kings
decisions.reason: The verb describes Solomon growing great, a process seen through the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: richer and wiser
decisions.reason: Readable turns the two nouns into adjectives, the plainest way to say the same thing.

records.source: וְכֹל֙ מַלְכֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ מְבַקְשִׁ֖ים אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה לִשְׁמֹ֨עַ֙ אֶת־חָכְמָת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּלִבּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And all [the] kings of the earth [were] seeking [the] face of Solomon to hear his wisdom which put God in his heart.
pieces: All the kings of the earth sought an audience with Solomon, to hear the wisdom God had put in his heart.

L.23: And all the kings of the earth were seeking the face of Solomon to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.

R.23: Kings from all over the world wanted to meet Solomon and hear the wisdom God had given him.

decisions.choice: all the kings of the earth: where 1 Kings 10:24 has "all the earth"
decisions.reason: Kings says the whole earth sought Solomon; Chronicles says the kings of the earth did, picking up "the kings of the earth" from verse 22. The rest of the verse is the same.

decisions.choice: seeking the face of Solomon: asking to come before him
decisions.reason: To seek a king's face is to seek an audience with him (Proverbs 29:26).

decisions.choice: the wisdom God had put in his heart: wisdom as a gift
decisions.reason: Solomon's wisdom is not his own achievement. God gave it, as he promised (1:12). The heart is the seat of understanding.

decisions.choice: sought an audience (Balanced); wanted to meet (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain the idiom of seeking his face.

records.source: וְהֵ֣ם מְבִיאִ֣ים אִ֣ישׁ מִנְחָת֡וֹ כְּלֵ֣י כֶסֶף֩ וּכְלֵ֨י זָהָ֤ב וּשְׂלָמוֹת֙ נֵ֣שֶׁק וּבְשָׂמִ֔ים סוּסִ֖ים וּפְרָדִ֑ים דְּבַר־שָׁנָ֖ה בְּשָׁנָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And they [were] bringing each his gift, articles of silver and articles of gold, and garments, weaponry, and spices, horses and mules, [the] matter of [a] year in [a] year.
pieces: Each of them brought a gift: articles of silver and gold, robes, weapons and spices, horses and mules, so much every year.

L.24: And they were bringing, each his gift: articles of silver and articles of gold, and garments, weapons, and spices, horses and mules, a year's portion year by year.

R.24: Year after year, each of them brought him gifts: things made of silver and gold, clothing, weapons, spices, horses and mules.

decisions.choice: were bringing, year by year: a regular yearly practice
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:25, which this verse repeats, the verb form describes a continuing custom, and "the matter of a year in a year" means a fixed amount each year. In Chronicles "they" are the kings of verse 23.

decisions.choice: his gift: an offering to honor the king
decisions.reason: The word is the common word for a gift or offering, used also of tribute paid to a ruler (17:11; Judges 3:15). Those who came to hear Solomon's wisdom came with gifts, as the queen of Sheba did.

decisions.choice: so much every year (Balanced); Year after year (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express the Hebrew "the matter of a year in a year" in plain English.

records.source: וַיְהִ֨י לִשְׁלֹמֹ֜ה אַרְבַּעַת֩ אֲלָפִ֨ים אֻֽרְי֤וֹת סוּסִים֙ וּמַרְכָּב֔וֹת וּשְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֖לֶף פָּרָשִׁ֑ים וַיַּנִּיחֵם֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י הָרֶ֔כֶב וְעִם־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: And were to Solomon four thousand stalls [of] horses and chariots, and two [and] ten thousand horsemen; and he stationed them in [the] cities of the chariotry and with the king in Jerusalem.
pieces: Solomon had 4,000 stalls for horses and chariots, and he had 12,000 horsemen, whom he stationed in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.

L.25: And Solomon had 4,000 stalls of horses and chariots, and 12,000 horsemen; and he stationed them in the cities of the chariots and with the king in Jerusalem.

R.25: Solomon had 4,000 stalls for his horses and chariots, and he had 12,000 horsemen. He kept some of them in the cities where his chariots were based, and some with him in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: 4,000 stalls, as the Hebrew text of Chronicles reads
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 5:6, which this verse echoes, has 40,000 stalls. The smaller number here fits the 1,400 chariots of 1 Kings 10:26 and 2 Chronicles 1:14 better. A copyist may have changed one of the numbers; see the note at 1 Kings 5:6.

decisions.choice: this verse joins 1 Kings 5:6 and 10:26
decisions.reason: Where 1 Kings 10:26 counts Solomon's 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen, Chronicles gives the stalls and horsemen from 1 Kings 5:6, then follows 10:26 in placing them in the chariot cities and in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: horsemen: the men who rode or drove, or perhaps the horses themselves
decisions.reason: The word usually means horsemen, but it can also mean horses for chariots, as the note at 1 Kings 5:6 explains.

decisions.choice: the chariot cities: towns with stables and barracks for the chariot force
decisions.reason: Solomon built store cities and towns for his chariots and horsemen (8:6).

decisions.choice: some ... and some with him
decisions.reason: Readable says that the force was divided between the chariot cities and Jerusalem, and says "with him" for "with the king", since the king is Solomon.

records.heading: The end of Solomon's reign

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י מוֹשֵׁ֖ל בְּכָל־הַמְּלָכִ֑ים מִן־הַנָּהָר֙ וְעַד־אֶ֣רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְעַ֖ד גְּב֥וּל מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And he was ruling over all the kings from the River and to [the] land of [the] Philistines and to [the] border of Egypt.
pieces: He ruled over all the kings from the Euphrates River to the land of the Philistines and as far as the border of Egypt.

L.26: And he was ruling over all the kings from the River to the land of the Philistines and as far as the border of Egypt.

R.26: He ruled over all the kings from the Euphrates River to the land of the Philistines and all the way to the border of Egypt.

decisions.choice: the same rule as 1 Kings 5:1
decisions.reason: Kings says Solomon ruled over "all the kingdoms"; Chronicles says "all the kings", and has "to" before "the land of the Philistines", which Kings leaves out. Kings goes on to say that they brought tribute; Chronicles has said so already (verses 23-24).

decisions.choice: the River: the Euphrates
decisions.reason: "The River" with the article names the Euphrates, as in the promise of the land to Abraham (Genesis 15:18). Solomon's rule reached the borders that promise named.

decisions.choice: the Euphrates River (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 5:1, Balanced and Readable name the river so that readers know which one "the River" means.

records.source: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ אֶת־הַכֶּ֛סֶף בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם כָּאֲבָנִ֑ים וְאֵ֣ת הָאֲרָזִ֗ים נָתַ֛ן כַּשִּׁקְמִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־בַּשְּׁפֵלָ֖ה לָרֹֽב׃
records.gloss: And made the king the silver in Jerusalem like stones, and the cedars he made like the sycamores which [are] in the Shephelah, for abundance.
pieces: The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and he made cedar as plentiful as the sycamore-fig trees of the Shephelah.

L.27: And the king made the silver in Jerusalem like stones, and the cedars he made like the sycamores that [are] in the Shephelah, for abundance.

R.27: The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones. Cedar wood became as plentiful as the fig trees that grow in the western foothills.

decisions.choice: like stones, like the sycamores: a deliberate overstatement
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 1 Kings 10:27 and 2 Chronicles 1:15. Silver and costly cedar from Lebanon became, with poetic exaggeration, as common as the most ordinary things in the land.

decisions.choice: the sycamores in the Shephelah: common fig trees of the low hills
decisions.reason: The sycamore fig bears small figs and gives cheap, ordinary timber (Amos 7:14). The Shephelah is the region of low hills between the coastal plain and the hill country of Judah.

decisions.choice: sycamore-fig trees of the Shephelah (Balanced); fig trees that grow in the western foothills (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 10:27, the English "sycamore" names a different tree, so Balanced says "sycamore-fig"; Readable explains the Shephelah by where it lies.

records.source: וּמוֹצִיאִ֨ים סוּסִ֧ים מִמִּצְרַ֛יִם לִשְׁלֹמֹ֖ה וּמִכָּל־הָאֲרָצֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And [they were] bringing out horses from Egypt for Solomon and from all the lands.
pieces: Horses were brought for Solomon from Egypt and from all the lands.

L.28: And they were bringing out horses from Egypt for Solomon, and from all the lands.

R.28: Solomon's horses were brought in from Egypt and from all the other lands.

decisions.choice: a shorter account than 1 Kings 10:28-29
decisions.reason: Kings names Egypt and Kue, gives the price of a chariot and a horse, and says that Solomon's traders sold them on to the kings of the Hittites and of Aram. Chronicles gave those details at 1:16-17; here it says only that horses came to Solomon from Egypt and from every land.

decisions.choice: horses from Egypt: what the law warned a king against
decisions.reason: The law of the king told him not to gather many horses or send the people back to Egypt to get them (Deuteronomy 17:16). The writer lists Solomon's horses without comment.

decisions.choice: were brought (Balanced); were brought in (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses "they were bringing out" with no named subject, a way of speaking of the trade in general; Balanced and Readable say it in the passive. Readable adds "other" since Egypt is one of the lands.

records.source: וּשְׁאָר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים וְהָאֲחֲרוֹנִ֑ים הֲלֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־דִּבְרֵי֙ נָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֔יא וְעַל־נְבוּאַ֞ת אֲחִיָּ֣ה הַשִּֽׁילוֹנִ֗י וּבַחֲזוֹת֙ יֶעְדּ֣וֹ הַחֹזֶ֔ה עַל־יָרָבְעָ֖ם בֶּן־נְבָֽט׃
records.gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Solomon, the first and the last, [are] not they written on [the] words of Nathan the prophet, and on [the] prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in [the] visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat?
pieces: The rest of the acts of Solomon, from first to last, are written in the records of Nathan the prophet, in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer about Jeroboam son of Nebat.

L.29: And the rest of the matters of Solomon, the first and the last, are they not written in the words of Nathan the prophet, and in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat?

R.29: Everything else Solomon did, from beginning to end, is written in the records of the prophet Nathan, in the prophecy of Ahijah from Shiloh, and in the visions about Jeroboam son of Nebat that Iddo the seer received. (A seer was a prophet to whom God gave visions.)

decisions.choice: different sources from 1 Kings 11:41
decisions.reason: Kings sends the reader to "the book of the matters of Solomon" for "all that he did, and his wisdom". Chronicles speaks of Solomon's matters "first and last" and names three prophetic writings instead: those of Nathan, Ahijah and Iddo.

decisions.choice: Nathan, Ahijah and Iddo: prophets whose writings recorded the reign
decisions.reason: Chronicles often names prophets as the writers of a king's history (1 Chronicles 29:29; 2 Chronicles 12:15; 13:22). Nathan spoke for God to David and helped make Solomon king (1 Chronicles 17; 1 Kings 1). Ahijah of Shiloh foretold that Jeroboam would rule ten tribes (1 Kings 11:29-39). Iddo's visions concerned Jeroboam. These writings have not survived.

decisions.choice: the seer: a prophet who received visions
decisions.reason: This word for "seer" comes from the verb "to see" and is used of a prophet to whom God showed things in visions, as of Gad, David's seer (1 Chronicles 21:9). Its sense is close to "prophet".

decisions.choice: are they not written?: a question that means "they are written"
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer yes. It is the usual way these books close a reign.

decisions.choice: the matters / the words of Nathan (Literal); the acts / the records of Nathan (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 11:41, Balanced says "the acts of Solomon" for his "matters". The same Hebrew word stands before Nathan's name, where it means his written account; Balanced and Readable say "records".

decisions.choice: are written
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the answer the question expects; Literal keeps the question.

decisions.choice: Ahijah from Shiloh; a prophet to whom God gave visions
decisions.reason: Readable says where Ahijah came from rather than using "Shilonite", and explains once what a seer was.

records.source: וַיִּמְלֹ֨ךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֧ה בִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם עַל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אַרְבָּעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And reigned Solomon in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years.
pieces: Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel for forty years.

L.30: And Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years.

R.30: Solomon ruled over all Israel from Jerusalem for forty years.

decisions.choice: a slight difference from 1 Kings 11:42
decisions.reason: Kings says "the days that Solomon reigned ... were forty years"; Chronicles says "Solomon reigned ... forty years". The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: forty years: the length of a generation
decisions.reason: David also reigned forty years (1 Chronicles 29:27). Forty is a common round number for a generation, and the figure may be rounded.

decisions.choice: all Israel: the whole united kingdom
decisions.reason: Solomon is the last king to rule over all twelve tribes. After him the kingdom divides (chapter 10).

records.source: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב שְׁלֹמֹה֙ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֔הוּ בְּעִ֖יר דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֑יו וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ רְחַבְעָ֥ם בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: And lay down Solomon with his fathers, and they buried him in [the] city of David his father; and reigned Rehoboam his son in his place.
pieces: Then Solomon rested with his ancestors and was buried in the City of David his father. And his son Rehoboam became king in his place.

L.31: And Solomon lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of David his father; and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.

R.31: Then Solomon died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David, his father's city. His son Rehoboam became king after him.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: The formula these books use for the death of a king, as at 1 Kings 11:43, which this verse repeats. There the Hebrew says "he was buried"; here it says "they buried him", with the same sense.

decisions.choice: the City of David: the old part of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The City of David was the stronghold David took from the Jebusites (1 Chronicles 11:5-7), where the kings of Judah were buried.

decisions.choice: Rehoboam his son: the next king
decisions.reason: Rehoboam's reign begins with the division of the kingdom (chapter 10).

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers / rested with his ancestors / died
decisions.reason: The death formula is worded the same way at each level throughout these books. Readable adds "with his ancestors" where the burial is named.

decisions.choice: was buried
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the wording of 1 Kings 11:43; "they buried him" has no particular subject, and the passive says the same thing.
